category: Camera Raw dialog - panels, tools and workflow
description: The controls of the Adobe Camera Raw plug-in as used from Photoshop (File > Open on raw/JPEG/HEIC, Filter > Camera Raw Filter, Bridge): the Edit panel groups (Profile, Basic, Curve, Detail, Color Mixer/Point Color, Color Grading, Optics, Geometry, Effects, Calibration, Lens Blur), the Masking, Healing/Remove, Crop, Red Eye and Presets/Snapshots panels, the AI Enhance features (Denoise, Raw Details, Super Resolution), reflection removal, HDR, workflow options, filmstrip sync and the Vectorscope. Version numbers refer to Camera Raw releases (16 = 2024, 17 = 2025, 18 = 2026).

tools.name: Camera Raw > Profile browser
tools.description: The rendering starting point applied before any slider: Adobe Raw profiles (Adobe Color, Monochrome, Landscape, Portrait, Neutral, Vivid, Standard), the image-adaptive Adobe Adaptive Color / Adaptive Monochrome profiles (16.4+, with an Amount slider and automatic per-image tone mapping), Camera Matching profiles that emulate the manufacturer's looks, and Creative/Artistic/Modern/Vintage/B&W profiles with an Amount slider. Legacy profiles remain for old process versions.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit panel > Profile menu / Browse (grid icon) > choose group > click profile; Amount slider for creative profiles

parameters.name: Profile menu
parameters.description: Quick list of favourites; click the grid to open the browser.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: 0-200 % strength for creative and adaptive profiles.

parameters.name: Favorites (star)
parameters.description: Pin profiles to the menu.

tools.example: Open a raw file, in Edit > Profile choose Browse, expand Adaptive and click Adobe Adaptive Color; lower Amount to 70 if the tone mapping is too strong, then fine-tune with Basic.
tools.notes: Profiles are not presets: they do not move sliders and can be combined with any preset. Adaptive profiles also work on JPEG/TIFF via Camera Raw Filter and for HDR output.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Basic > White Balance
tools.description: Sets the colour temperature interpretation of the raw data: presets (As Shot, Auto, Daylight, Cloudy, Shade, Tungsten, Fluorescent, Flash, Custom) for raw files (JPEGs get As Shot/Auto/Custom only), Temperature (2000-50000 K for raw, -100..100 for rendered files) and Tint (-150..150 green/magenta), plus the White Balance eyedropper (I) that neutralises the clicked point. Mask-local white balance is available in the Masking panel.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Basic > White Balance menu / Temperature / Tint / eyedropper (I)

parameters.name: White Balance preset
parameters.description: As Shot, Auto, Daylight, Cloudy, Shade, Tungsten, Fluorescent, Flash, Custom.

parameters.name: Temperature
parameters.description: Kelvin for raw; relative -100..100 for JPEG/TIFF.

parameters.name: Tint
parameters.description: -150 (green) to +150 (magenta).

parameters.name: Eyedropper
parameters.description: Click a neutral grey area; a single click sets both Temperature and Tint.

tools.example: Press I, click the grey card in the test frame, then Ctrl+A in the filmstrip and Synchronize > White Balance to apply to the whole set.
tools.notes: Raw white balance is lossless; on JPEG it re-maps already-rendered colours with less latitude. Auto WB in ACR 16+ uses the AI 'Auto' model.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Basic > Light (Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks)
tools.description: The tonal core of Camera Raw: Exposure (-5..+5 EV, midtone-weighted), Contrast (-100..100), Highlights and Shadows (-100..100, recover blown/blocked areas), Whites and Blacks (-100..100, set the clipping points; Alt-drag shows clipping). Auto applies the Sensei auto-tone model to all six plus Vibrance/Saturation. Clipping warnings toggle with J (shadows) and O (highlights) or the histogram triangles.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Basic > Light group; Auto button; Alt-drag Whites/Blacks for clipping preview

parameters.name: Exposure
parameters.description: -5 to +5 stops.

parameters.name: Contrast
parameters.description: -100 to +100 midtone contrast.

parameters.name: Highlights / Shadows
parameters.description: -100 to +100 recovery of bright/dark ranges.

parameters.name: Whites / Blacks
parameters.description: -100 to +100 end-point clipping controls.

parameters.name: Auto
parameters.description: AI auto-tone; click the Auto button (no default shortcut in Camera Raw).

tools.example: Click Auto, then pull Highlights to -60 and Whites to +10 for a bright sky; Alt-drag Blacks until the first pixels appear to set a clean black point.
tools.notes: Adjust in order Exposure > Contrast > Highlights/Shadows > Whites/Blacks; Whites/Blacks interact with Highlights/Shadows. Works identically in the Camera Raw Filter on 8/16-bit layers (less headroom than raw).

tools.name: Camera Raw > Basic > Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, Vibrance and Saturation
tools.description: Presence and colour intensity: Texture (-100..100) sharpens or smooths medium-frequency detail without halos (skin, bark), Clarity (-100..100) boosts midtone local contrast (stronger, adds punch), Dehaze (-100..100) cuts or adds atmospheric haze by estimating scene depth, Vibrance (-100..100) saturates muted colours while protecting skin tones, Saturation (-100..100) scales all colours equally.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Basic > Effects (Texture, Clarity, Dehaze) and Color (Vibrance, Saturation)

parameters.name: Texture
parameters.description: Fine/medium detail contrast; negative for skin smoothing.

parameters.name: Clarity
parameters.description: Midtone local contrast; can darken and halo at high values.

parameters.name: Dehaze
parameters.description: Haze removal (+) or fog effect (-); shifts colour toward blue at extremes.

parameters.name: Vibrance / Saturation
parameters.description: Smart vs linear saturation.

tools.example: Landscape: Dehaze +25, Clarity +15, Texture +10, Vibrance +20; then use a Subject mask with Texture -20 on a portrait.
tools.notes: The same three Effects sliders became native Photoshop adjustment layers (Clarity and Dehaze, Grain) in 27.3, and Color and Vibrance is a 27.3.1 adjustment layer.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Curve panel
tools.description: Tone curve with three editing modes: Parametric (Highlights, Lights, Darks, Shadows sliders with movable region splits), Point Curve (free-form points on the composite curve with a targeted-adjustment tool) and per-channel Red, Green, Blue point curves for colour grading and split-tone effects. Curve presets (Linear, Medium Contrast, Strong Contrast) can be saved.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Curve > Parametric / Point / Red / Green / Blue tabs

parameters.name: Parametric sliders
parameters.description: Highlights, Lights, Darks, Shadows -100..100 with region split handles.

parameters.name: Point curve
parameters.description: Click to add points and drag them, or use the targeted adjustment tool to drag directly on the image.

parameters.name: Channel curves
parameters.description: Independent RGB curves for colour casts and cross-processing.

tools.example: Point curve: add a point at (64, 72) and (192, 184) for a gentle S; Blue curve: lift the black point slightly for a faded film look.
tools.notes: Curves apply after Basic and before Color Grading. Masks have their own local curves since ACR 15.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Detail panel (Sharpening and Noise Reduction)
tools.description: Capture sharpening - Amount (0-150), Radius (0.5-3.0), Detail (0-100, halo suppression vs fine detail) and Masking (0-100; Alt-drag shows the edge mask) - plus manual Noise Reduction: Luminance (0-100) with Detail and Contrast, and Color (0-100) with Detail and Smoothness. The panel also hosts the AI Denoise button (ACR 15.3+). Judge at 100 % zoom.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Detail > Sharpening / Noise Reduction; Alt-drag Masking, Radius, Detail for visualisations

parameters.name: Amount / Radius / Detail / Masking
parameters.description: Sharpening strength, halo width, high-frequency emphasis, edge mask threshold.

parameters.name: Luminance / Detail / Contrast
parameters.description: Luminance NR strength and its detail/contrast preservation.

parameters.name: Color / Detail / Smoothness
parameters.description: Chroma NR strength, edge preservation, blotch smoothing.

parameters.name: Denoise... (AI)
parameters.description: Opens the Enhance dialog with Denoise selected.

tools.example: Portrait at ISO 3200: Amount 40, Radius 1.0, Detail 25, Masking 60 (Alt-drag until only edges are white); Luminance 25, Color 25 - or click Denoise for the AI model instead.
tools.notes: Output sharpening for screen/print is separate (Workflow Options). Denoise output is a new DNG; manual NR sliders are disabled on Denoised files.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Color Mixer and Point Color
tools.description: Color Mixer offers HSL (Hue, Saturation, Luminance tabs for eight colour ranges) and Color (per-swatch editing) modes with a targeted-adjustment tool that drags on the image; Point Color (ACR 16+) samples an exact colour with an eyedropper and adjusts its Hue, Saturation and Luminance with adjustable Range and Refine (hue/saturation/luminance spread) controls, and shows a Visualize Range overlay. Point Color is the precise tool for brand colours and skin tones; HSL for broad ranges.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Color Mixer > HSL / Color / Point Color tabs

parameters.name: HSL tabs
parameters.description: Hue, Saturation, Luminance -100..100 for Reds, Oranges, Yellows, Greens, Aquas, Blues, Purples, Magentas.

parameters.name: Point Color
parameters.description: Eyedropper samples up to 8 colours; Hue/Saturation/Luminance shift; Range and Refine sliders; Visualize Range.

tools.example: Point Color: sample the sky blue, Hue -8 toward cyan, Saturation +10, Range 40; check with Visualize Range that only the sky is affected.
tools.notes: Point Color also exists inside masks. HSL Luminance is the cleanest way to darken a sky without banding.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Color Grading panel
tools.description: Three-way colour wheels (Shadows, Midtones, Highlights) plus a Global wheel, each with Hue, Saturation and Luminance, and Blending (how much the ranges overlap) and Balance (shifts the midpoint between shadows and highlights). Successor to Split Toning, used for teal-orange looks, warm highlights/cool shadows and monochrome tints.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Color Grading > 3-way / Shadows / Midtones / Highlights / Global views

parameters.name: Wheels
parameters.description: Drag inside the wheel for hue/saturation; slider beneath for luminance; Alt-drag for finer control.

parameters.name: Blending
parameters.description: 0-100 overlap between tonal ranges.

parameters.name: Balance
parameters.description: -100..100 bias toward shadows or highlights.

tools.example: Shadows: hue 215, saturation 12; Highlights: hue 45, saturation 10; Blending 50, Balance +10 for a subtle cinematic grade.
tools.notes: Grading is applied after the Curve; keep saturation low (under 20) for natural results.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Optics panel
tools.description: Lens corrections: Remove Chromatic Aberration (automatic lateral CA), Use Profile Corrections (distortion and vignetting from the lens profile database with Distortion and Vignetting amount sliders and manual Make/Model/Profile selection), and Defringe (Purple/Green Amount and Hue ranges plus an eyedropper for axial CA). Profiles are embedded automatically for many mirrorless cameras.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Optics > Remove Chromatic Aberration / Use Profile Corrections / Defringe

parameters.name: Remove Chromatic Aberration
parameters.description: One-click lateral CA removal.

parameters.name: Use Profile Corrections
parameters.description: Setup Default/Auto/Custom; Lens Profile Make, Model, Profile; Distortion and Vignetting 0-200 %.

parameters.name: Defringe
parameters.description: Purple Amount/Hue, Green Amount/Hue; eyedropper to sample fringes.

tools.example: Tick both checkboxes, then click the Defringe eyedropper on a purple fringe at a backlit edge; reduce Vignetting to 50 if you like some corner falloff.
tools.notes: Lens profiles are shared with Lightroom and Photoshop's Lens Correction filter; missing lenses can be profiled with the Adobe Lens Profile Creator (legacy).

tools.name: Camera Raw > Geometry panel (Upright)
tools.description: Perspective correction: Upright modes Off, Auto (balanced), Level (horizon), Vertical (converging verticals), Full (both), and Guided (draw 2-4 lines that should be vertical/horizontal), plus Manual transforms - Vertical, Horizontal, Rotate, Aspect, Scale, X/Y Offset - and Constrain Crop to remove the transparent wedges. A Loupe/Grid overlay helps alignment.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Geometry > Upright buttons / Guided (draw lines) / Manual Transforms / Constrain Crop

parameters.name: Upright
parameters.description: Off, Auto, Level, Vertical, Full, Guided.

parameters.name: Manual transforms
parameters.description: Vertical, Horizontal (-100..100), Rotate (-10..10), Aspect (-100..100), Scale (50-150 %), X/Y Offset.

parameters.name: Constrain Crop
parameters.description: Auto-crop the corrected image to the largest rectangle.

tools.example: Architecture: enable Use Profile Corrections first, click Guided, draw two lines along building edges and one along the horizon, tick Constrain Crop.
tools.notes: Apply lens profile corrections before Upright for accurate results. Upright analysis can be re-run after cropping changes.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Effects panel (Grain and Vignetting)
tools.description: Post-crop Vignetting (Amount -100..100, Midpoint, Roundness, Feather, Highlights; Style: Highlight Priority, Color Priority, Paint Overlay) and film Grain (Amount, Size, Roughness) applied after cropping and independent of the lens profile vignette. Grain here is the model reused by the Photoshop Grain adjustment layer (27.3).
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Effects > Grain / Vignetting

parameters.name: Grain: Amount / Size / Roughness
parameters.description: 0-100 each; Size >25 adds blur to the grain.

parameters.name: Vignetting: Amount / Midpoint / Roundness / Feather / Highlights
parameters.description: Negative darkens, positive lightens corners; Highlights keeps bright areas from being darkened.

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Highlight Priority (best), Color Priority, Paint Overlay.

tools.example: Vignetting Amount -20, Midpoint 40, Feather 70, Highlights 30; Grain Amount 15, Size 25, Roughness 50.
tools.notes: Post-crop vignette follows the crop; use Optics > Vignetting to correct the lens, Effects to add a creative one.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Calibration panel
tools.description: Low-level colour interpretation: Process Version (Version 6 current; older 1-5 retained for compatibility), Shadows Tint, and Hue/Saturation for the Red, Green and Blue primaries, which change how the raw channels are mapped before every other adjustment. Used for camera-to-camera matching and for strong 'teal-orange' primaries looks.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Calibration > Process / Shadows / Red, Green, Blue Primary

parameters.name: Process
parameters.description: Version 6 (2023, current), 5 (2018), 4, 3, 2, 1; updating an old version may change the look.

parameters.name: Shadows Tint
parameters.description: -100..100 green/magenta in shadows.

parameters.name: Red / Green / Blue Primary Hue and Saturation

tools.example: Blue Primary Saturation +20 and Red Primary Hue -5 to push a look toward the popular orange/teal separation without touching HSL.
tools.notes: Primaries adjustments are global and affect skin; combine with masks for control. Process version changes are recorded in the XMP.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Lens Blur panel
tools.description: AI depth-of-field simulation (ACR 16+): Camera Raw estimates a depth map (or uses an embedded one from phones/depth-capable cameras), then Blur Amount (0-100), Bokeh style (Circle, Bubble, 5-Blade, Ring, Cat Eye, Anamorphic oval - 17+), Boost (highlight bokeh brightness), Focal Range with a visual range selector and Focus/Blur refine brushes let you re-focus the image. Visualize Depth shows the map.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Edit > Lens Blur > Apply > Blur Amount / Bokeh / Boost / Focal Range / Refine (Focus, Blur brushes) / Visualize Depth

parameters.name: Bokeh
parameters.description: Circle, Bubble, 5-Blade, Ring, Cat Eye, Anamorphic.

parameters.name: Focal Range
parameters.description: Point/range picker on the image or the depth slider; Auto focuses on the subject.

parameters.name: Refine
parameters.description: Focus and Blur brushes to correct depth-map errors.

tools.example: Click Apply, choose Bokeh Anamorphic, Blur Amount 60, click the subject's eye to set focus, then paint Focus over misdetected hair strands.
tools.notes: Depth estimation is slow on large files; GPU recommended. Available in the Camera Raw Filter for JPEGs too.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Masking panel
tools.description: Local adjustments with AI and manual masks: Subject, Sky, Background, Objects (brush or rectangle to detect an object), People (per-person and per-feature: face skin, body skin, eyebrows, eye sclera, iris and pupil, lips, teeth, hair, clothes), Landscape (17+: sky, water, vegetation, mountains, architecture, natural ground, artificial ground), Brush, Linear Gradient (bidirectional since 18.5), Radial Gradient, Color Range, Luminance Range, Depth Range; masks combine with Add/Subtract/Intersect and each mask carries a full set of Light, Color, Effects, Detail, Curve and Point Color sliders.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Masking (M) > Create New Mask > type > adjust sliders; Add / Subtract; Masks panel lists and toggles them; Show Overlay checkbox and overlay colour options

parameters.name: AI masks
parameters.description: Subject, Sky, Background, Objects, People, Landscape - computed on demand, re-computable with Update.

parameters.name: Manual masks
parameters.description: Brush (size, feather, flow, density, auto mask), Linear Gradient, Radial Gradient.

parameters.name: Range masks
parameters.description: Color Range (eyedropper + refine), Luminance Range (min/max + feather), Depth Range (needs depth data).

parameters.name: Mask options
parameters.description: Invert, duplicate, rename, overlay colour/mode, Amount slider per mask.

tools.example: Create New Mask > Sky; Exposure -0.7, Dehaze +15; Subtract > Luminance Range to exclude clouds; then Create New Mask > People > Face Skin with Texture -25.
tools.notes: Masks are stored in XMP and survive round-trips to Lightroom. Select Subject/Sky in Photoshop use the same models.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Healing panel (Remove, Heal, Clone, Generative Remove)
tools.description: Retouching inside Camera Raw: the Remove brush (Content-Aware, ACR 14.3+) fills painted areas from surrounding content, Heal blends a sampled source, Clone copies it exactly; Generative Remove (17+) uses Firefly for larger objects; Visualize Spots shows sensor dust; automatic dust spot detection (17) and blemish detection (18.5, Remove > Blemishes) find and fix spots in one click. Each stroke stays editable with size, feather and opacity.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Remove tool (B) > Mode: Remove / Heal / Clone / Generative Remove; Visualize Spots; Dust / Blemishes auto-detect

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Remove (content-aware), Heal, Clone, Generative Remove (cloud, credits).

parameters.name: Size / Feather / Opacity
parameters.description: Brush controls.

parameters.name: Visualize Spots
parameters.description: High-pass threshold view to reveal dust.

parameters.name: Auto dust removal / Blemishes
parameters.description: One-click detection and removal (17 / 18.5).

tools.example: Tick Visualize Spots, drag the threshold until dust shows, click Remove Dust (17+), then paint over a distracting sign with Generative Remove.
tools.notes: Heal/Clone sources can be dragged after the fact. Generative Remove results are stored as generative edits in the XMP settings and are re-rendered if the edit is changed.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Reflection Removal
tools.description: AI removal of reflections photographed through glass (windows, display cases, cars): introduced as a Technology Preview in ACR 17.1 (December 2024) for raw files, improved and moved into the Remove tool's Distraction Removal section (ACR 18 / Lightroom 2026) with support for more file types, and added to Photoshop's own Remove tool in 27.6. A slider chooses how much of the reflection to remove or even to keep only the reflection.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Remove tool > Distraction Removal > Reflections > Apply; strength slider   (17.1: Preferences > Technology Previews > Reflection Removal)

parameters.name: Reflections toggle / Apply
parameters.description: Runs the model (cloud or on-device depending on version).

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: -100 (keep only reflection) to +100 (fully removed).

tools.example: Open a shop-window photo, Remove tool > Distraction Removal > Reflections > Apply, set Amount 100, then Heal any residual ghosting.
tools.notes: Works best on plate-glass reflections with the subject behind the glass; mirrors and water reflections are out of scope. Requires a raw file in 17.1; JPEG/HEIC support arrived later.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Crop & Rotate tool
tools.description: Non-destructive crop with aspect presets (Original, As Shot, 1:1, 4:5, 5:7, 2:3, 16:9, custom), Angle slider and Straighten tool (drag along a horizon; Auto uses Upright Level), Flip Horizontal/Vertical, and Constrain to Image after geometry corrections. The crop is stored in XMP and can be revisited any time.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Crop & Rotate (C) > aspect menu / drag handles / Angle / Straighten (Shift+drag) / Flip

parameters.name: Aspect
parameters.description: Presets or custom ratio; lock icon keeps the ratio.

parameters.name: Angle / Straighten
parameters.description: -45 to +45 degrees; draw a line to level.

parameters.name: Flip Horizontal / Vertical
parameters.description: Mirror the image.

tools.example: Press C, choose 16:9, drag the frame, then Shift-drag along the horizon to straighten; press Enter.
tools.notes: Cropping in Camera Raw does not reduce the raw data; Workflow Options > Image Sizing determines the output pixel size.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Red Eye tool
tools.description: Fixes flash red-eye in people (Red Eye) and the green/white reflections of animal eyes (Pet Eye) by dragging a box over each eye; Pupil Size and Darken sliders refine the result, and Pet Eye can add a catchlight.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Red Eye (E) > Type: Red Eye / Pet Eye > drag over the eye > Pupil Size / Darken / Add Catchlight

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Red Eye or Pet Eye.

parameters.name: Pupil Size / Darken
parameters.description: Size of the corrected pupil and its darkness.

parameters.name: Add Catchlight (Pet Eye)
parameters.description: Adds a specular highlight.

tools.example: Press E, choose Pet Eye, drag a box over each glowing eye, tick Add Catchlight.
tools.notes: Photoshop's own Red Eye tool (under Healing) does the same on rendered pixels.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Presets panel and Adaptive Presets
tools.description: One-click looks: Premium presets grouped by Portraits (Deep Skin, Medium Skin, Light Skin), Style, Subject, Cinematic, Travel, Video, Vintage, Black & White, Curve, Grain, Sharpening, Vignetting...; Adaptive presets (Subject, Sky, Portrait) that create AI masks and apply local edits; user presets (New Preset from current settings, with checkboxes for which groups to include, ISO-adaptive presets) and an Amount slider (0-200 %) to scale any preset. Presets are .xmp files shared with Lightroom.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Presets (Shift+P) > browse groups > hover to preview > click; Amount slider; ... menu > Create Preset / Import Presets

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: 0-200 % strength of the applied preset (ACR 14+).

parameters.name: Create Preset
parameters.description: Name, group, and which settings to store (Treatment & Profile, Basic, Curve, Detail, Color Mixer, Color Grading, Optics, Geometry, Effects, Calibration, Masks, Crop); ISO Adaptive option.

parameters.name: Import Presets / Profiles
parameters.description: Load .xmp preset files or .zip bundles; legacy .lrtemplate is converted.

tools.example: Presets > Adaptive: Portrait > 'Soft Skin' - it builds a Face Skin mask automatically; drag Amount to 60.
tools.notes: User presets live in %AppData%\Adobe\CameraRaw\Settings (Windows). Presets referencing masks re-run the AI detection per image.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Snapshots and Versions
tools.description: Snapshots store named copies of the complete edit state inside the XMP so alternative looks can be recalled at any time (Create Snapshot, Update with Current Settings, Rename, Delete); versions in Lightroom map to the same data. Use them to keep a colour and a B&W interpretation of one raw file, or to bookmark before an experiment.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > Snapshots (Shift+S) > + (Create Snapshot) > name; click a snapshot to restore; right-click > Update with Current Settings
tools.example: Finish the colour grade, create snapshot 'Color v1'; switch Profile to Adobe Monochrome, adjust, create 'B&W v1'; toggle between them before opening into Photoshop.
tools.notes: Snapshots are part of the sidecar/DNG metadata and survive Lightroom round trips. The Camera Raw Filter (as a Smart Filter) keeps snapshots per filter instance.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Enhance (Denoise, Raw Details, Super Resolution)
tools.description: AI image enhancement that writes a new DNG: Denoise (ACR 15.3+, amount slider 0-100) removes luminance and colour noise with a trained model far better than the manual sliders; Raw Details (formerly Enhance Details) improves demosaicing for fine detail and reduces artefacts; Super Resolution doubles the linear resolution (4x pixels) with AI upsampling. Batch-enhance from the filmstrip; the output '-Enhanced-NR.dng' opens with the same edits.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > right-click image (or Detail panel) > Enhance... > tick Denoise (amount) / Raw Details / Super Resolution > Enhance

parameters.name: Denoise
parameters.description: Amount 0-100; preview crop shows before/after; includes Raw Details.

parameters.name: Raw Details
parameters.description: Demosaic improvement for Bayer/X-Trans raws.

parameters.name: Super Resolution
parameters.description: 2x width and height; includes Raw Details; in Camera Raw it needs a raw/DNG source (Lightroom also accepts JPEG/TIFF).

parameters.name: Estimated time
parameters.description: Shown in the dialog; GPU strongly recommended.

tools.example: Select 20 high-ISO raws in the filmstrip, Enhance > Denoise 50 > Enhance; the DNGs appear beside the originals with '-Enhanced-NR'.
tools.notes: Denoise DNGs are 3-4x larger than the raw. Photoshop's Neural Filter Super Zoom is the equivalent for rendered images.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Workflow Options
tools.description: The output settings used when an image leaves Camera Raw for Photoshop: Preset, Color Space (sRGB, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto RGB, Display P3, Rec. 2020 with intent), Depth (8 or 16 bits/channel), Image Sizing (native, presets, long/short edge, megapixels, resolution, Preserve Details resampling), Output Sharpening (Screen, Glossy Paper, Matte Paper at Low/Standard/High), and 'Open in Photoshop as Smart Objects'. Click the blue link at the bottom of the dialog to open it.
tools.usage: Camera Raw dialog > click the workflow summary link (bottom) or the gear/preferences > Workflow

parameters.name: Color Space / Intent / Depth
parameters.description: Output profile, rendering intent (for output profiles), 8 or 16-bit.

parameters.name: Image Sizing
parameters.description: Resize to Fit: Width & Height, Dimensions, Long Side, Short Side, Megapixels, Percentage; Don't Enlarge; Resolution.

parameters.name: Output Sharpening
parameters.description: Sharpen For: Screen / Glossy Paper / Matte Paper; Amount Low/Standard/High.

parameters.name: Open in Photoshop as Smart Objects
parameters.description: Makes Open become Open Object by default.

tools.example: Set ProPhoto RGB, 16 Bits/Channel, Sharpen For Screen Standard, tick Open in Photoshop as Smart Objects - a wide-gamut editing workflow where Camera Raw can be re-opened by double-clicking the layer.
tools.notes: Shift-click Open toggles between Open Image and Open Object for one time. Camera Raw Filter output ignores these (it renders into the existing document).

tools.name: Camera Raw > HDR editing and output
tools.description: Since ACR 15.0 (2022) raw files can be edited in HDR: the HDR toggle in the histogram header enables headroom above SDR white (shown as a highlight region in the histogram) when a supported HDR display is present, Visualize HDR shows the ranges, and Adjust SDR rendition controls the SDR fallback; output can be an HDR-capable format (AVIF, JPEG XL, 16-bit PNG/TIFF, gain-map JPEG in Lightroom) or a 32-bit Photoshop document. ACR 18 refined the HDR pipeline for HDR displays.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > histogram header > HDR toggle; Visualize HDR; Settings > SDR rendition; Save Image with an HDR-capable format, or Open into Photoshop as a 32-bit document

parameters.name: HDR toggle
parameters.description: Switch the pipeline to HDR; requires HDR display and OS support to view.

parameters.name: Visualize HDR
parameters.description: Overlay of SDR/HDR ranges and clipping.

parameters.name: SDR rendition
parameters.description: Adjust how the image maps to standard displays (Brightness, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Clarity).

tools.example: Enable HDR, set Whites and Exposure so the sun's disc sits within the HDR headroom, then Save Image as AVIF with HDR output for the web.
tools.notes: Opening an HDR-edited raw into Photoshop delivers a 32-bit document; most Photoshop tools are limited at 32-bit. Windows needs HDR turned on in Display settings.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Filmstrip, Synchronize and Save Image
tools.description: When several files are opened together the filmstrip (left) lists them with ratings, flags and colour labels; Select All / Synchronize (Sync Settings dialog with checkboxes per group) copies edits across, Copy/Paste Edit Settings does the same selectively, and Save Image... (bottom-left) batch-exports the selection to JPEG, TIFF, PSD, PNG or DNG with naming, sizing, sharpening and metadata options without opening Photoshop. Done applies the edits and closes; Open opens the selected files.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > filmstrip > Ctrl+A > ... menu > Sync Settings (Alt+S) / Copy Edit Settings / Paste Edit Settings; Save Image... (button at bottom left)

parameters.name: Sync Settings dialog
parameters.description: Choose which groups to copy (White Balance, Basic, Curve, Detail, Color Mixer, Color Grading, Optics, Geometry, Effects, Calibration, Masks, Crop, Spot Removal).

parameters.name: Save Image
parameters.description: Destination, File Naming tokens, Format (JPEG quality / TIFF compression / PSD / PNG / DNG options), Color Space, Image Sizing, Output Sharpening, Metadata.

parameters.name: Done / Open / Cancel
parameters.description: Apply and close; open into Photoshop; discard.

tools.example: Edit the first frame of a series, Ctrl+A in the filmstrip, Sync Settings with everything except Crop and Masks ticked, then Save Image > JPEG 85 %, Long Side 2048 px, Sharpen for Screen.
tools.notes: Camera Raw stores ratings/labels in XMP, visible in Bridge. Save Image runs in the background while you keep editing.

tools.name: Camera Raw > Histogram, clipping warnings, Before/After views and Vectorscope
tools.description: Evaluation aids: the histogram (RGB overlay, clipping triangles for shadows/highlights, click to toggle the on-image warnings, J/O keys), the readout of RGB values under the pointer, Before/After view modes (Y: side-by-side, split, single toggle; Q cycles) with swap/copy buttons, zoom presets and the Vectorscope (ACR 18.5, August 2026) that plots hue/saturation distribution for objective colour evaluation and skin-tone line checks.
tools.usage: Camera Raw > histogram (top right) > clipping triangles / J / O; Before/After button (Y) and Q to cycle layouts; Vectorscope tab (18.5+)

parameters.name: Clipping warnings
parameters.description: Blue overlay = shadow clipping, red = highlight clipping.

parameters.name: Before/After
parameters.description: Left/Right, Left/Right Split, Top/Bottom, Top/Bottom Split, single view toggle (backslash key).

parameters.name: Vectorscope
parameters.description: Hue/saturation scatter with skin-tone reference; 18.5+.

tools.example: Press O to show highlight clipping, lower Whites until the red disappears from the sky; press Y and Q to compare layouts.
tools.notes: Clipping warnings reflect the output colour space chosen in Workflow Options. The Vectorscope also appears in Lightroom Classic 2026.
